title: The Second Company Mona Ataya Had Not Planned to Start
dek: In late 2011 a Dubai mother of three put a bilingual shop for mothers online, before the Gulf had the couriers or payment systems to make it easy.

story.event: Launching an online shop for mothers in the Gulf
story.summary: In late 2011 Mona Ataya, a Bayt.com executive and mother of three, launched Mumzworld.com in Dubai with co-founder Leena Khalil, a bilingual online shop for mother, baby and child products, at a time when Gulf e-commerce lacked reliable couriers and payment gateways. The company built its own delivery fleet, accepted cash on delivery and raised money from angels and Alghanim Industries in early 2012. In June 2021 Saudi Arabia's Tamer Group agreed to buy a majority stake.
paragraphs: In November 2011 Mona Ataya put Mumzworld.com online in English and Arabic, with about 15,000 products for children from newborns to twelve-year-olds. She had introduced the idea a month earlier on Bayt.com, the Dubai recruitment site she had helped her brother build since 2000, and she started it with a co-founder, Leena Khalil. A mother of three, Ataya later said a second business "wasn't in my agenda".

The idea came from her own shopping. In stores, she said, she had felt "not given enough choice or information about products and brands", and some children's goods cost four or five times more in the UAE than abroad. She had taken two years off work after her twins were born and four after her third child. Being an investor in the company she worked for, she said, had given her that flexibility, without which she "wouldn't have been able to start Mumzworld".

She also knew what was missing. Online shopping in the region was in its infancy: Ataya named the need for a dependable courier system, a workable payment gateway and staff with the right skills, and shoppers were wary of buying online. She built around the gaps rather than waiting for them to close. Customers could pay cash on delivery, and by 2013 the company ran its own fleet of about twenty messengers in the UAE, using outside couriers only for overflow. Ataya said she had been told a first funding round would take at least a year; by her account it was oversubscribed within six weeks. Angel investors and Kuwait's Alghanim Industries put money in early in 2012, and in 2013 she opened the next round to women investors only.

By 2013 at least six rival shops had found delivery hard enough to become storefronts on Mumzworld instead. In 2017 the company opened its own warehouse. By 2021 it had raised about $50 million, and that June Saudi Arabia's Tamer Group agreed to buy a majority stake, with Ataya and Khalil staying on as shareholders and board members. The work had its cost. In 2017 Ataya called it "a 24-hour job, 365 days a year"; she has also said she never switches off.

quote.text: We must not force crops from rich fields, for an unbroken course of heavy crops will soon exhaust their fertility, and so also the liveliness of our minds will be destroyed by unceasing labour, but they will recover their strength after a short period of rest and relief
quote.work: Of Peace of Mind (De Tranquillitate Animi), in the Minor Dialogues
quote.source_title: Minor Dialogues, Together With the Dialogue on Clemency, tr. Aubrey Stewart, Project Gutenberg eBook #64576
quote.connection: Ataya built a company into years already full of children and work, and she describes it as a job with no off-switch. Seneca, writing to a restless friend, says a field cropped without pause gives less in time. Mumzworld grew regardless; the quote leaves open what that pace costs.

reflection: Ataya is open about two things that are easy to skip over. Her second company was not part of any plan, and what made it possible was flexibility: earlier years in which she could step away from work for her children without losing her place.

You may not have that kind of flexibility, and the work in front of you may never offer a natural stopping point. Seneca's field is not a reproach. It is a reminder that the hours you keep for sleep, for the people at home, or for nothing in particular are not stolen from the work. They are part of what lets it keep growing.
invitation: Choose one evening this week, and an hour on it after which you will not open work messages. Tell someone close to you which evening it is.

cross_checks.claim: Mumzworld was founded in late 2011 by Mona Ataya and Leena Khalil.
Mumzworld launched with about 15,000 products when Gulf online retail was in its infancy.
Payment and delivery infrastructure were early obstacles, and customers could pay cash on delivery.
A later funding round was opened only to women investors.
In June 2021 Tamer Group agreed to buy a majority stake, with the founders staying on.

research_notes: Launch month: Ataya told Images RetailME (2013) that she set up the site in November 2011, a month after introducing the concept on Bayt.com; Wamda (2018) gives October 2011 and Wamda (2013) and Khaleej Times (2021) say late 2011. The story uses November for the site going live and 'a month earlier' for the announcement, matching her own account. Leena Khalil is named as co-founder by Wamda (2018, 2021) and Khaleej Times (2021); the 2013 interviews mention only Ataya, so the story names Khalil without describing her role in the first weeks. Children: Harbus quotes Ataya as a mother of three; Wamda (2013) says twins then aged ten and a third child aged six; Gulf News mentions twin boys. Infobae (2022), which repeats some of these details, was not used because it wrongly dates Bayt.com's founding to 2011. The first round's speed (oversubscribed in six weeks, six term sheets) is Ataya's own account in a Harvard Business School interview reported by The Harbus and is attributed to her; Wamda (2013) independently records a Series A in early 2012 from angels and Alghanim Industries, with no amount. Product counts vary by date and source (90,000 in 2013; 120,000 in Khaleej Times and 140,000 in The National, both 2017; 200,000 in 2018; 250,000 in 2021), as do brand counts (6,000 in 2017, 5,500 in 2021), so the story gives only the launch figure. The $50 million total raised comes from Wamda (2021) alone and is stated as 'about'. The six competitors becoming storefronts was reported by Wamda in 2013 from the company. Ataya's description of working '18 hours a day, 365 days a year' and never switching off is from a Gulf News interview whose page is marked as last updated in July 2022 (the original publication date is not shown), so the story does not date it. The Seneca passage is from his advice to Serenus on keeping the mind at peace; it is applied by analogy.
